title: Optimizing Symmetry Informed Probabilistic Error Cancellation
authors: Tom O'Leary, Daniel J. Egger, Dieter Jaksch
abstract: We show that combining quantum error detection (QED) with probabilistic error cancellation (PEC) gives more accurate and lower-variance estimates than PEC alone, provided that the symmetry measurements required for QED are carefully chosen. Because noisy symmetry measurements can negate the benefits of the PEC+QED approach, we cast the selection of measurement configurations as a classical optimization problem that systematically suppresses the impact of noise. Applying optimized PEC+QED to GHZ-state output distributions and to simulating the time-dynamics of a generalized superfast encoded Fermi-Hubbard model, we find consistent improvements over PEC. For GHZ states, the optimization over symmetry measurement configurations is essential for achieving an advantage. For the Fermi-Hubbard model, PEC+QED improves observable estimation on a $2 \times 2$ lattice and for larger systems the mitigation overheads can be reduced by measuring only subsets of stabilizers. Our results demonstrate the importance of circuit-specific tailoring of QEM techniques and that fault-tolerant design principles may already provide value for near-term devices.
summary: The paper presents a method combining Quantum Error Detection (QED) and Probabilistic Error Cancellation (PEC) to estimate expectation values from noisy quantum circuits. By optimizing which symmetries are measured, the technique systematically reduces estimation variance compared to using PEC or QED in isolation. This is demonstrated successfully when simulating dynamics for models like the Fermi-Hubbard model.
main_problem: The primary goal is to improve quantum estimation accuracy and reduce variance when estimating expectation values of noisy quantum circuits, surpassing standard Probabilistic Error Cancellation (PEC) by integrating Quantum Error Detection (QED). This is achieved through optimizing the selection of symmetry measurements.
main_result: Combining QED with PEC provides more accurate and lower-variance estimates than either method alone, especially when symmetries are optimized. The approach successfully mitigates errors in simulating complex models like the Fermi-Hubbard model on a lattice.
method: The authors combine PEC (using inverse channels $\Lambda^{-1}$) with QED (by post-selecting on error-free measurements) and treat the selection of symmetry measurement configurations as a classical optimization problem to suppress noise impact.
model_or_system: The work applies to general noisy quantum circuits, specifically demonstrating utility for GHZ-state output distributions and simulating the time-dynamics of a generalized superfast encoded Fermi-Hubbard model on lattices.

paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework by defining the combined estimator, deriving cost functions based on error detection probabilities ($p_{	ext{no-det}}$), and then applies this optimization procedure to benchmark systems like GHZ state preparation and the Fermi-Hubbard model dynamics.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses resource estimation for simulating strongly correlated electron models (like the FH model) under realistic noise conditions, providing tailored error mitigation techniques crucial for near-term quantum simulation hardware.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Overview of PEC+QED. (a) In a circuit with L-layers of noisy gates, detectable errors are mitigated by measuring symmetries using circuit USYM and post-selecting, retaining circuits with probability pno-det. Remaining errors are mitigated by applying PEC to cancel undetectable noise Λ−1 l,u at each layer l, incurring a sampling cost γ2 undet,l which multiplies per layer. Mitigating noise in USYM introduces a sampling cost CSYM. (b) Given a set of possible symmetries to measure S = {Si}4 i=1, we seek a configuration C ⊂S with minimal cost. Each symmetry Si ∈C has a detectable error set Di and incurs cost µi, while each undetected error Ej incurs cost λj.
